bpLabel: Fieldstrip Best Practices guide. No manufacturer manual exists for this model, so we built this from general best practices for this type of firearm. It does not represent manufacturer data. If you obtain the factory manual, follow it over this guide. Never take a firearm further apart than this guide goes unless its maker documents it.
cleanIntro:
No manual from Perazzi exists for this model. A break-action gun is built to come apart into three pieces — stock and action, barrels, forend — and that take-down is the same on every gun of the kind. This guide clears the gun, takes it down that far and no further, and cleans it with the barrels off.

Listed in Fieldstrip as 12 GA. The gauge and chamber length marked on the gun itself is the one that counts — not this guide, and not the listing.

steps.title: Ammunition out of the room, muzzle somewhere safe
steps.action: Before you start, put every loose shell, loaded magazine and box of ammunition in another room — a cleaning bench with live rounds on it is where unintended discharges happen. Keep the muzzle pointed where a shot would hurt no one, and keep your finger outside the trigger guard the whole time. Wear eye protection whenever you use solvent or work near a spring, and work where the air moves.
steps.prose: A safety, if yours has one, is never a substitute for an empty chamber, and nothing in this guide relies on one.

steps.title: Open the action and let the barrels drop
steps.action: Push the top lever across and let the barrels drop open on the hinge. Lift out any shells the extractors raise, or catch any the ejectors throw. Open, the gun shows its own state plainly — which is why it stays open until this guide tells you to close it.

steps.title: Look through every barrel, feel every chamber
steps.action: Look through each barrel from the breech end against the light, then run a fingertip into every chamber the gun has. Do it twice. A shell left in a chamber is the one thing this whole guide exists to catch.
steps.prose: ⛔ If a shell will not come out of a chamber, stop: never pry it out with a tool — contact Perazzi.

steps.title: Forend off by its latch
steps.action: With the gun open, look under the forend for its release: a lever on its underside, a button at its front tip, or nothing at all on a forend that snaps on. Work the lever or press the button and lift the forend away from the barrels; a snap-on forend comes away with a firm pull at its front end. Put it aside on a soft cloth.
steps.prose: ⛔ If a screw holds the forend on, or it will not release by hand, stop here: clean the gun with the forend on and the action open.

steps.title: Barrels off the hinge
steps.action: With the forend off and the action still open, lift the barrels upward and forward off the hinge pin; they come free once their hooks clear it. Lay them down on a soft cloth — never stand a pair of barrels on their muzzles.

steps.title: That is the whole take-down
steps.action: Nothing else comes apart. The stock, the trigger group — even on a gun made for it to drop out — the ejectors and extractors, the choke tubes and anything held by a screw all stay exactly as they are: those are work for Perazzi.
steps.prose: Choke tubes do need taking out now and then so they cannot seize, but how, and with which wrench, is a question for Perazzi.

steps.title: Each bore and each chamber, from the breech
steps.action: Brush each bore wet with bore solvent from the breech end, a few passes, then dry patches until they come out clean. Clean each chamber with a chamber brush — plastic and carbon build a ring at the chamber mouth that makes shells stick. Finish with a lightly oiled patch for storage, and run a dry patch through before you shoot.
steps.prose: The crown — the edge of the muzzle — is what decides where the shot goes; a rod dragged across it does lasting harm.

steps.title: Breech face, extractors and the hinge
steps.action: Wipe the standing breech — the flat face of the action with the firing-pin holes in it — with a cloth and a little solvent, and keep oil out of those holes. Wipe the extractors or ejectors in place at the barrels' breech end; they stay where they are. Then a thin film of gun grease or oil on the hinge pin, the barrel hooks and the forend iron's bearing face, where metal turns on metal.

steps.title: The outside, and how it is stored
steps.action: Wipe the outside with a lightly oiled cloth, and keep solvent off wood, finishes and optics. Store it dry, out of a closed case or bag while it is still damp, and look it over for rust at every clean.

steps.title: Look for the things that mean stop
steps.action: Hold the barrel up to the light and look through it: you want a clean, unbroken bore with no obstruction, no bulge and no dark ring. Look over the barrels, the action and the stock for cracks, dents in the barrels, and for anything loose or missing. A screw or pin that has worked loose is reported, not tightened — how tight it should be is a question for Perazzi.
steps.prose: Any one of these means the gun is not fired until Perazzi has seen it.

deepAbsentReason: There is no deep clean for the Perazzi MX10, and this guide will not invent one. No manual from Perazzi exists for this model, so nothing about the inside of it can be known from a document. Anything that needs more than this guide goes to Perazzi, not onto the bench.

cleaning.name: BORES & CHAMBERS
tasks: Each bore brushed wet from the breech end, then dry patches until clean
Each chamber with a chamber brush — the plastic ring at the mouth
A lightly oiled patch for storage; a dry patch before the next shot

cleaning.name: ACTION & HINGE
tasks: ⛔ No oil into the firing-pin holes
Extractors or ejectors wiped in place
A thin film of grease or oil on the hinge pin, the barrel hooks and the forend iron

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wiped with a lightly oiled cloth
No solvent on wood, finishes or optics

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: Stored dry — never shut in a closed case while damp
Looked over for rust at every clean

reassembly: Action open: the barrels lowered onto the hinge pin with their hooks engaged, then swung closed — the top lever returns to the centre.
The forend back on: hooked at its rear, then pressed up until its latch clicks or the snap-on forend seats.
Open and close the gun once: it should open smoothly and close with the lever returning to the centre.
fncheck: Every chamber empty. The gun opens fully, closes, and locks with the top lever back at the centre. A safety, if fitted, moves through its positions. This check never asks you to pull a trigger; whether a gun of this kind may be dry-fired, with snap caps or without, is a question for Perazzi.
